items.text: From 1 July 2023, psychiatrists approved by the TGA under the Authorised Prescriber Scheme, after a human research ethics committee approves, can prescribe MDMA for post-traumatic stress disorder. For every other use MDMA stays a prohibited substance (Schedule 9), largely limited to clinical trials.
From 1 July 2023, authorised psychiatrists can prescribe psilocybin for treatment-resistant depression under the same scheme. For every other use it stays a prohibited substance (Schedule 9).

From 1 July 2024, nicotine vapes can be sold only in pharmacies. From 1 October 2024, adults 18 and over can buy therapeutic vapes with up to 20 mg/mL nicotine from a pharmacy without a prescription, subject to state and territory laws; under 18s need a prescription.

Travellers 18 and over can bring up to 4 kg of kava powder into Australia in accompanied baggage. Different arrangements apply in the Northern Territory, and commercial imports for food use need an import permit.

laws.rule: On return, complete the Incoming Passenger Card accurately (a digital Australia Travel Declaration is being piloted on some Qantas flights). Adults can bring AUD 900 of general goods duty free; over the allowance, duty and tax apply to every item of that type. Goods claimed under the Tourist Refund Scheme must be declared.

Declare food, plant material and animal products, including goods you took overseas and brought back. Clean hiking, fishing and camping gear and footwear. Declared goods are not penalised under the Biosecurity Act 2015 even if refused; false or missing declarations can bring an infringement notice of up to AUD 7,280 or prosecution.
Smartraveller offers free email and SMS updates for each destination, and says that if you can't afford travel insurance, you can't afford to travel.

Consular help is not a legal right and may be limited if your actions were illegal or repeatedly reckless. DFAT may replace passports (fee), give lists of doctors and lawyers, check on you if detained, contact family with consent and provide some notarial and voting services. It can't give legal advice, intervene in foreign courts, get you out of prison, pay bail, fines or medical bills, or arrange visas or work permits.
Australian citizens and residents can be prosecuted in Australia for child sex offences committed overseas (Criminal Code Division 272); the AFP investigates.
Bribing a foreign public official is an offence for Australians anywhere (Criminal Code s 70.2), with up to 10 years' imprisonment for individuals.

Supplying technology on the Defence and Strategic Goods List overseas, including by email, cloud access or screen-sharing, generally needs a Defence permit unless an exemption applies. Relevant only if your work touches controlled technology.

You generally stay an Australian resident for tax if you go overseas temporarily and do not set up a permanent home elsewhere; moving from country to country does not create one. Residents declare worldwide income and may claim a foreign income tax offset. You can lodge from overseas through myTax (set myGov sign-in to work abroad).

Medicare does not cover you overseas. Reciprocal health care agreements with 11 countries (Belgium, Finland, Ireland, Italy, Malta, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Slovenia, Sweden, the UK) may cover urgent care, usually with a co-payment; they don't cover evacuation and don't replace travel insurance. Carry your passport and a current Medicare card.
Strict rules apply to taking PBS medicines overseas; carry them for personal use and check they are legal at the destination.

Federal voting is not compulsory while overseas, but tell the AEC (overseas notification form) or you will be asked to explain. Enrolled voters leaving for longer can register as an overseas elector up to 3 months before or within 3 years after leaving, valid 6 years; vote by post or in person at selected missions.
